statement: Every subspace must contain the zero vector; this follows directly from the scalar-multiplication rule by choosing c = 0.
quotes: First fact: Every subspace contains the zero vector.
but it follows directly from rule (ii).

statement: Z is the vector space consisting only of the zero vector; it is the smallest possible vector space and, inside R^3, the subspace containing just (0,0,0).
quotes: Z The vector space that consists only of a zero vector.
The vector space Z contains exactly one vector (zero). No space can do without that zero vector.

statement: The row space of A is written C(A^T), the column space of A transpose: transposing turns the rows of A into columns, so the same numbers now span a subspace of R^n. The left nullspace is written N(A^T).
quotes: The row space of A is $C ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$ . It is the column space of
Instead of the rows of A, look at the columns of $A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$ . Same numbers, but now in the column space

statement: The column space of A consists of all linear combinations of the columns of A, i.e. all vectors Ax; it is a subspace of R^m.
quotes: The column space consists of all linear combinations of the columns.
It is a vector space made up of column vectors.

statement: The two subspace requirements combine into one: a subspace containing v and w must contain every linear combination cv + dw.
quotes: A subspace containing v and w must contain all linear combinations
In short, all linear combinations stay in the subspace.

statement: A plane through the origin in R^3 is a subspace: sums and scalar multiples of in-plane vectors stay in the plane. Planes that miss the origin are not subspaces.
quotes: If we add two vectors in the plane, their sum is in the plane.
Planes that don't contain the origin fail those tests. Those planes are not subspaces.

statement: A set of vectors spans a space if their linear combinations fill the space. The columns of a matrix span its column space; they might be dependent.
quotes: DEFINITION A set of vectors spans a space if their linear combinations fill the space.
The vectors $v _ { 1 } , \ldots , v _ { r }$ span a space if their combinations fill that space.
The column space is spanned by the columns.

statement: A line through the origin is a subspace: multiplying a vector on the line by a scalar or adding two vectors on the line keeps you on the line, but the line must pass through (0,0,0).
quotes: Lines through the origin are also subspaces.
the subspace SS is the line through v.

statement: C(A) denotes the column space of A: the set of all linear combinations of the columns of A.
quotes: The column space of A is denoted by
C(A) contains not just then columns of A, but all their combinations Ax.

statement: The row space of a matrix is the subspace of R^n spanned by its rows: all combinations of the rows. It is the column space of A transpose, and it is a subspace of R^n while the column space lives in R^m.
quotes: DEFINITION The row space of a matrix is the subspace of $\mathbf { R } ^ { n }$ spanned by the rows.
The columns span the column space. Here is a new subspace-which is spanned by the rows.
The row space contains all combinations of the rows. This row space of A is the column space of $A ^ { \mathrm { T } }$

statement: The system Ax = b is solvable if and only if b lies in the column space of A; then b is a combination of the columns and the coefficients give a solution x.
quotes: The right side b has to be in the column space produced by A on the left side, or no solution!
is solvable if and only if b is in the column space of A.

statement: A subspace of a vector space is a set of vectors (including 0) closed under addition and scalar multiplication, so all linear combinations stay in the set.
quotes: A subspace of a vector space is a set of vectors (including 0) that satisfies two requirements
Those operations leave us in the subspace.
